Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

RESY 0.3

Breaking changes — function renames

  • prepare_eunis() split into resy_check_eunis() (pure validation) and resy_harmonize_eunis() (geographic enrichment + taxonomy).
  • check_taxonomy() → resy_check_taxonomy()
  • check_format() → resy_check_data()
  • resy_validate_expert() → resy_validate_esy()

Internal changes

  • resy_parse_expert(), resy_parse_json(), resy_show_vegtypes() are now internal (unexported). Use resy_load_expert() as the single entry point for loading any expert system.
  • resy_eval_type() is now internal. Use resy_eval_plot(res, p, type = ) to evaluate one type on one plot.
  • Geographic helpers (check_ecoregions, check_country, check_coast_dunes, check_coordinates) consolidated into internal functions in internal_eunis_geo.R under the .resy_assign_* / .resy_check_* naming convention.
  • RDS format support removed. Expert systems are imported from .txt and stored as .json. resy_available_classifications() no longer returns an expert_rds column.
  • resy_expert_path() format argument is now c("json", "txt") only.
  • The GIS layers in data/ are read on first use and kept for the session. Attaching the package reads none of them, and repeated resy_check_data() calls on the 200 example plots take 0.07 s instead of 0.17 s.
  • The shiny app’s Classify button calls resy_classify().
  • tibble moved from Imports to Suggests; methods is no longer imported.

New

  • resy_check_eunis() — validates plot data against EUNIS structural requirements before harmonization, returning list(ok, errors, warnings).
  • New general vignette vignette("RESY") covering classification with both EUNIS and Apennine-test expert systems without EUNIS-specific geographic steps.
  • Package help page ?RESY with an overview of the workflow.
  • Taxonomy crosswalk for plot data named under a general backbone: resy_read_synonyms() returns the synonym table of an expert system or reads your own crosswalk, resy_canonical_species() returns the canonical ESy names, and resy_resolve_taxa() maps a name column to them. A name that resolves to nothing stays NA and is flagged, never replaced by a guess. resy_classify(resolve_taxa = TRUE) runs the resolution before classifying; the default FALSE classifies the names as given. See vignette("taxonomy").
  • resy_clean_names() removes author citations from taxon names.
  • All three published EUNIS-ESy releases ship with the package as their original .txt files, xz-compressed (expert.txt.xz: 160, 168 and 640 KB for 2020-06-08, 2021-06-01 and 2025-10-03; the content has the MD5 of the Zenodo file). The 2025-10-03 release replaces the expert.json.xz shipped before, which kept only the last declaration of an aggregate declared twice in the release (Mentha longifolia, Dactylorhiza majalis) and left out two aggregates. The synonym table anchored on 2025-10-03 has 67,005 pairs instead of 67,018: the restored members make 13 synonyms either names of the expert system or ambiguous. resy_load_expert(scheme = "EUNIS", version = ) and resy_classify(version = ) choose the release; the default remains the newest. Expert files of either format may be xz-compressed in a classification store.
  • resy_add_classification(scheme = "EUNIS", version = ) without file downloads a published release from Zenodo, checks it against its SHA-256 checksum and stores it in the user store. The releases are declared in inst/extdata/classifications/releases.csv, from which data-raw/build_registry.R builds the getaca registry inst/getaca/registry.rds. The registry is also read from the repository on GitHub, so a release published later becomes available without a new version of RESY. Downloading requires getaca (Suggests).
  • resy_provenance() reports which release a parsed expert system or a classification result rests on: scheme, version, file, MD5 checksum, DOI of the release, whether the file is byte-identical to the published .txt, and, for resy_classify(resolve_taxa = TRUE), the build of the synonym layer. A file passed as expertfile is recognised as a release by its content. The version element of a resy_classify() result now holds the version used rather than the argument given.
  • resy_diff_expert() lists the aggregates, species groups and types that were added, removed or changed between two expert systems, for example two EUNIS-ESy releases given by version. A .txt and a .json file can be compared with each other.
  • NON conditions on ##C and ##D groups are evaluated. The right-hand side is the highest total cover among the other groups of the same set, the statistic the left-hand side takes for these groups; ##Q is unchanged. The EUNIS-ESy release of 2021-06-01 uses one such condition (type N), which stopped classification with that release before.
  • The RESY App offers the EUNIS-ESy releases in a menu, names the release and its DOI in the description and under the results, and adds expert_system and expert_version columns to the downloaded table.
  • The RESY Maker (articles/maker.html, linked from the RESY App) builds an expert system in the browser on one screen: the types, the rule of the type shown put together from conditions as blocks, and beside it the species groups, the species list and the test plots. A group is made, named and filled from the condition that needs it, or dragged into a rule. After every change RESY classifies a set of test plots (the example plots or your own files) and the page shows the number of plots in which each condition and each rule holds; selecting a plot marks the conditions it meets and misses. The page opens on the draft kept in the browser or on the Apennine example; an empty system, a shipped system or a .json or .txt file is opened from the top bar. A system is exported as .json or .txt or handed to the RESY App. The .txt file is read back and compared with the .json file before it is offered. Types and groups are deleted from their lists, species are ticked (Shift for a range) and removed together and can be put back, Save downloads the system as a file and Clear empties it after a confirmation.
  • The RESY App and the RESY Maker are both in the navigation bar and share one window: the page that was opened loads the other tool in the background, so going from one to the other, with or without an expert system, does not start R again.
  • The RESY App keeps each expert system it has read, so choosing a system again shows its description at once instead of reading the file again (EUNIS-ESy 2025-10-03: 1.6 s to under 0.1 s).
  • The explanation of a plot in the RESY App and the RESY Maker lists a species that is not in the expert system under the name written in the plot data.
  • resy_load_expert() reads a .txt file whose types have a letter as priority (0-9, A-Z, a-z, as in a .json file). Such a file passed resy_validate_esy() but could not be loaded.
  • resy_read_expert() reads the species aggregation section of a large .txt file about 2.5 times faster (EUNIS-ESy 2025-10-03: 2.5 s to 1.0 s), with the same result.
  • A type code that fills the five-character code field of a .txt header is read without the description that follows it directly: N15!!, not N15!!Atlantic. Trailing ! marks number further rules of a type; the three EUNIS-ESy releases each have five such headers (N15!!, N16!!, N17!!, T1C!!, T1D!!).
  • Reading a .txt expert system is about 19 times faster (9.7 s to 0.5 s for the three EUNIS-ESy releases), with an identical result. Loading EUNIS-ESy 2025-10-03 takes 0.3 s from the .txt and 0.14 s from the former .json. The file is read once for both the parser and the checksum that resy_provenance() reports.
  • resy_load_expert() keeps each loaded system in RESY’s cache directory (tools::R_user_dir("RESY", "cache")) and restores it on later loads of the same file: EUNIS-ESy 2025-10-03 then loads in 0.08 s, the three EUNIS-ESy releases in 0.14 s. A cached copy is used only while the file keeps its size and modification time and the same installed RESY loads it; a new copy replaces the older ones of that file. options(RESY.cache = FALSE) turns the cache off and options(RESY.cache_dir =) moves it.
  • An #SC comparison receives its EXCEPT clause by the literal text of its condition. A condition holding + (a discriminating group such as #SC +12 Conifers) was left without the clause, and one holding | also added it to other expressions that share part of its text. No shipped expert system has such a condition, so their results are unchanged.
  • Formulas and membership expressions are turned into R code by matching each bracketed condition and each side of a comparison as a whole, instead of replacing every condition text in turn. The result is identical for all shipped expert systems, and RESY no longer depends on stringi.
  • resy_expert_path() returns by default the file a classification is stored in, whichever its format; format = "json" or "txt" still asks for one.
  • resy_check_taxonomy() also counts as known the species that a species group or a membership condition names without Section 1 listing them. The 2020 and 2021 EUNIS-ESy releases list only aggregates in Section 1, so a species such as Fagus sylvatica was reported unmatched and the RESY App, which drops unmatched names, left 1,609 of the 3,580 example records out (1,573 for 2021). The App now classifies 196 of the 200 example plots with either release, as resy_classify() does.
  • resy_load_expert() and resy_classify() gain location. By default a classification is looked up first in the user store, where resy_add_classification() puts it, then among the shipped classifications.
  • resy_harmonize_eunis() writes DEG_LAT and DEG_LON. source_crs can be left out for coordinates in degrees (read as EPSG:4326), and coordinates in any other CRS are converted. It warns when no site falls inside the country base map. resy_check_eunis() and resy_check_data() read degree coordinates the same way.
  • resy_classify() warns when the expert system has conditions on header columns that header lacks; those conditions are evaluated as if the value were 0.
  • resy_validate_esy() resolves group references the way the classifier does. The EUNIS-ESy release of 2025-10-03 now gives 3 warnings instead of 234.
  • The synonyms come from six taxonomic backbones (Euro+Med, WFO, GBIF, COL, ITIS, NCBI), collected once by data-raw/build_synonyms.R into a layer that serves every expert system and release. resy_read_synonyms(), resy_canonical_species() and resy_resolve_taxa() take an expert (by default the newest EUNIS release) and fit the layer to its species names, so each release gets its own synonym table; resy_classify(resolve_taxa = TRUE) uses the expert system it classifies with. A synonym that points to two names the expert system evaluates differently, counting the members of its aggregates, is resolved by Euro+Med or stays unresolved. For EUNIS 2025-10-03 the table has 67,018 synonym pairs. The build date and the release of each backbone are in inst/extdata/esy_synonym_layer_build.csv and esy_synonym_layer_backbones.csv. An accepted_in column names the backbones that list the synonym as an accepted name under the same author as the supporting synonym rows.
  • The canonical names of an expert system are the names its classifier evaluates: the aggregates of Section 1, and the species that a species group or a membership condition names and that no aggregate includes. resy_resolve_taxa() leaves every species name the expert system uses untouched, including the names of species groups and conditions.
  • resy_resolve_taxa() matches a name a second time with its author citation removed (resy_clean_names()) when it does not match as given. These matches are labelled "cleaned_exact" and "cleaned_synonym" in taxon_confidence.
  • resy_check_taxonomy() and resy_resolve_taxa() both return a resy_taxa data frame with a logical matched column. resy_check_taxonomy() names its columns scientificName (as submitted), TaxonName (canonical) and matched. Printing a resy_taxa table describes its columns and counts the matches; summary() gives the counts per name and per record, the records by match type, and the unmatched names grouped into genus only, below species level and species. resy_summarize_taxa() is removed; use summary() on the result of resy_resolve_taxa(). With resolve_taxa = TRUE, resy_classify() stores that summary as taxon_resolution.
  • resy_candidates(wide = TRUE) returns one row per plot: plot_id, its classification, then type_1, priority_1, type_2, priority_2, …, highest priority first. Plots without candidates are kept with NA.
  • resy_eval_plot() explains a plot’s classification in plain words: the types whose rules hold with their priorities, the type chosen, and the plot’s species with cover. It then lists the lower-level types the plot did not reach, closest first, and shows the closest in full: its rule with numbered conditions, and for each condition whether it is met, the plot’s value, the required value and the species behind it. type = shows any type the same way; lower = FALSE turns the list off. The group_names column is no longer added to the species output.
  • Plot data can use Darwin Core column names: eventID for the plot ID, scientificName for the species, organismQuantity with a percent-cover organismQuantityType for the cover, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude and country for the site, and minimumElevationInMeters / maximumElevationInMeters for Altitude (m), which is also read from a column Altitude. species_col in resy_classify() and resy_resolve_taxa() and col in resy_check_taxonomy() default to NULL, which uses TaxonName, then scientificName.

Fixes

  • The .txt expert-file parser keeps the last member of the last group in section 2 when the section ends on it, and no longer stores blank lines as group or aggregation members. An aggregation without members is now an empty character vector. Classifications from the EUNIS-ESy releases of 2020, 2021 and 2025 are unchanged.
  • Header conditions ($$C, $$N) are evaluated on each plot’s own header row.
  • Classifying a single plot with an expert system that has exactly one numeric header condition ($$N) no longer overwrites the value of the system’s first membership condition with the header value. resy_eval_plot() output in the RESY App, which classifies the selected plot alone, showed that value, for example a total cover of 10.7% (the plot’s longitude) in place of 87.9%.
  • resy_validate_esy() reads a .txt and a .json file into the same parts (group keys and type definitions) and checks them with one set of rules, so a system gets the same report in either format. Three files that defined the validator a second time, and whose older definitions were the ones in use, are removed. With them go the false warnings they gave: header columns ($$C, $$N), set tags (+01), groups joined by | and group names with spaces were reported as undefined groups, 277 times for the EUNIS-ESy release of 2025-10-03, which now gets three warnings (tab characters, the condition #TC Cliff-ferns GR05 of type P2N, the duplicate code T3M).
  • resy_validate_esy() reports a type without a formula as an error in a .txt file too (RESY cannot read such a file; it was a warning), a Section 3 header without a code, a file without any type, and an empty type description in a .txt file.
  • inst/extdata/example_mini_expert_file.txt holds two type definitions in Section 3; it held two lines that are no definitions, and RESY could not load it.
  • A membership condition is replaced in a formula together with its angle brackets, so text outside a condition that equals a condition is left as it is. The compiled formulas of the shipped systems are unchanged. Before, the header rows were used in the order of header, so a plot read another plot’s header values unless header and obs listed the plots in the same order. On the 200-plot EUNIS example 13 plots change type.
  • Total cover (#T$) and highest cover (#$$) conditions are filled by plot id. Before, their values landed on the wrong plots when obs was not sorted by plot id.
  • Groups combined with | (e.g. #TC Trees|#TC Shrubs GR 15) are evaluated as one condition on the union of the groups, not as separate conditions joined by OR. On the 200-plot EUNIS example 11 plots change type.
  • Before, EUNIS conditions on DEG_LAT and DEG_LON read 0 because resy_harmonize_eunis() did not write these columns. On the 200-plot EUNIS example 15 plots change type.
  • resy_eval_plot() looks up a plot in the classifier’s plot order, not in the row order of header, and reports the responsible taxa of #TC ... GR n conditions, which were NA.
  • resy_aggregate_taxa() works with an expert system that has no aggregations.
  • resy_candidates(top_n = ) keeps the candidates with the highest priority. Before, it kept those with the lowest, so top_n = 1 returned for example F (priority 2) for a plot classified as FB (priority 5).
  • resy_classify() stops when obs has no species_col column. Before, it classified every plot as unclassified (?). A species_col other than TaxonName is used even when obs also has a TaxonName column.
  • resy_add_classification() stores the metadata of a .txt input as metadata.json; it was named expert.json, which resy_load_expert() then tried to read as the expert system. overwrite = TRUE removes the previous files.

Documentation

  • vignette("taxonomy") opens with the three steps (resolve, inspect, classify) and states the build date and backbone versions of the shipped synonym table, with a table and a figure of how many backbones support each pair. Its classify example resolves names against the vocabulary of the expert system it classifies with.
  • vignette("RESY") shows the printed result and the summary() of resy_check_taxonomy().
  • The EUNIS vignette lists Markus Bauer, Mariasole Calbi and Gilles Colling as authors and links to the EUNIS page on the EEA Datahub.
  • The Altitude vignette’s sections start at level 2, below the title.
  • The help pages of the GIS datasets give their names, sources and titles.

Licence and authors

  • The licence is unchanged (MIT). LICENSE holds the CRAN template (year and copyright holder) and the full text is in LICENSE.md. Both name all four authors as copyright holders.

Package size

  • GIS reference layers reduced (data-raw/simplify_gis.R rebuilds all of them), cutting data/ from 9.5 MB to 1.9 MB and the source tarball to 4.2 MB, below the CRAN 5 MB limit. coastline_regions, ecoregions2017 and dunes_bohn_* are simplified with rmapshaper and rounded to a 10 m grid. The coast, ecoregion and dune assignments of the bundled 200-plot example are the same as with the full-resolution layers. Of 16,521 random points 4 to 6 km from the full-resolution coastline, 99 get a different coast; of 20,000 random points within 2 km of an ecoregion or dune polygon border, 349 get a different ecoregion and 69 a different dune assignment. europe_resolution_1 (country lookup) keeps all vertices, rounded to a 1 m grid (3.0 MB to 1.1 MB); none of 858 test points within 2 km of a border or coast changes country. europe_resolution_60 is unchanged.

RESY 0.2

  • Added resy_read_expert(), resy_write_expert(), resy_expert_tree(), resy_write_expert_html(), resy_view_expert(), and resy_eunis_names() for lossless reading, writing, and hierarchical inspection of expert-system files.
  • Added resy_parse_json() for direct parsing of structured JSON expert files.
  • prepare_eunis() now returns a named list with sites and species_checked. A new parsed argument is required when run_taxonomy = TRUE.
  • check_taxonomy() signature updated: obs, parsed, col replace the former species argument.
  • resy_available_classifications() now discovers both package-bundled and user-added classification files.
  • resy_expert_path() gains "json" as a supported format.
  • Bug fixes and documentation updates throughout.
